title.narrative: Laws, policies, MoAs for prosecution and adjudication of maritime crimes are developed, strengthened, adopted.

description.narrative: OVERALL OBJECTIVE: Improve maritime security and safety in the Gulf of Guinea in the ECOWAS Region. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVE: (1) governance and law enforcement frameworks are strengthened and prosecution and adjudication of maritime crimes are more successful at regional and national levels The main goal of the Programme is having ECOWAS member states in a position to prosecute piracy and other maritime crime cases in line with the Yaoundé Code of Conduct and implementing the EIMS, with particular reference to actions 1.4, 1.5, 2.3 and 2.5. In order to achieve this, UNODC will be building on already conducted legal reform work initiatives, training and mentoring for prosecutors, judges and law enforcement officials in five ECOWAS pilot countries, including Benin, Ghana, Côte dIvoire, Nigeria, and Togo. In addition, some new countries will be undergoing a legal assessment including Cabo Verde, Guinea, Guinea Bissau, Liberia, Senegal, Sierra Leone and The Gambia. UNODC will also support legal cooperation, developing MoUs for improving quality and quantity of prosecutions. Actions will include: building capacity for prosecutions, improving regional cooperation at investigation and prosecution levels, legal reforms where needed in Gulf of Guinea countries and ad hoc / on demand legal support to existing cases. In pursuing such an objective, the Project will refer to EIMS and set its action, within the limits of its mandate, on supporting ECOWAS in implementing its EIMS, with particular regards to actions 1.43, 1.5, 2.3 and 2.5. The Project conceived to contribute to the integrated approach connecting security, governance and development promoted by the EU Strategy for the Gulf of Guinea and in line with the EU Maritime Security Strategy pursuing to ensure freedom, safety and security of navigation, including actions against piracy, and coherence between the activities of various organizations, notably in the fisheries, environment and transport fields. The Project further contributes to the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. It contributes primarily to the progressive achievement of SDG 8: Promoting inclusive and sustainable economic growth and Goal 14: Conserve and sustainably use the oceans, but also promotes progress towards Goal 1: Ending poverty; Goal 10: Reduce inequality; Goal 16: Promote peace, justice and strong institution. , peaceful and inclusive societies.
